item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00198","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C04","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 plausibly supplied a concrete two-section drafting template: first, statutory functions are designated or delegated to the Attorney General; second, the Attorney General may pass their exercise to Department of Justice officers or agencies. The child reproduces this same sequence and closely corresponding language, adapted from Trading With the Enemy Act functions to seizure authority under Title VI of the 1917 act. C04 and C20 share Attorney General designation machinery, but neither matches the child's compact designation-plus-Justice-officer redelegation structure as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Attorney General is hereby designated under section 1 of Title VI of the act of June 15, 1917 ... as a person duly authorized to seize and detain arms or munitions of war or other articles","parent_excerpt":"the Attorney General shall carry out the functions provided for in that subsection ... and functions under the said subsection are hereby delegated to the Attorney General, and the Attorney General is hereby designated thereunder","explanation":"Both provisions designate the Attorney General to exercise authority conferred by a specifically cited statute."},{"child_excerpt":"The authority conferred upon the Attorney General by section 1 of this order may be exercised by any officer of the Department of Justice designated for such purpose by the Attorney General.","parent_excerpt":"The Attorney General may delegate to any officer and agency of the Department of Justice such of his functions under this order as he may deem necessary.","explanation":"This is a close linguistic and structural match: each second section authorizes the Attorney General to assign the order's newly conferred functions to Justice Department subordinates."}]}
